# FR: topic analysis of the last three attempts (Sep 2025, Jan 2026, May 2026)

Status: researcher notes for the revision app. Everything in the tables is read from the ICAI papers; wording marked *app-written* is not ICAI text.

## 0. Sources, how to read this, and checks

- Sep 2025 and Jan 2026: ICAI suggested-answer booklets (`work/papers/fr_sep25_qp_2.txt`, `work/papers/fr_jan26_qp_2.txt`); question text read from the text layer, marks as printed.
- May 2026: now taken from ICAI's suggested-answer booklet (`work/papers/fr_may26_sa_1.txt`, same layout as Jan 2026, published at icai.org/post/sugg-ans-final-may2026). Marks were re-checked against the booklet and agree with the scanned paper (`fr_may26_qp_1.pdf`) for all 29 rows. May 2026 concept labels now use ICAI's answer key and answer text (the key is quoted as 'ICAI key'). Standard paragraphs: ICAI's May 2026 answers name very few: **Ind AS 101 para D18** (Q5(b)), **AS 16 para 4(b)** (previous-GAAP premium on redemption, Q5(b)), and **Ind AS 34 read with Ind AS 8** (Q2(b)(iii)). All other May 2026 answers cite the standard by number only, so no further paragraph numbers are given.
- Two things in ICAI's May 2026 text worth knowing: MCQ CS-I Q5 has a key of 'B OR D' (both accepted); the Q5(b) answer calls the company 'Sigma Ltd.' although the question says Gama Ltd.; and in Q4(a) ICAI computes plan-asset income at the expected-return rates printed in the question (the app-written note: Ind AS 19 itself measures interest on plan assets at the discount rate; follow ICAI's layout if the question gives expected returns).
- ICAI's own corrections in the Sep 2025 booklet (read 'loan notes' as 'preference shares'; read 'annual market yield on high quality corporate bonds' as 'market yields on government bonds'; MCQ 15 'no correct option') and Jan 2026 (MCQ 7 accepts both A and C) are noted in the rows.
- *App-written* concept labels name what the question tests. Where a label says 'ICAI answer' or 'ICAI key' it was read from the suggested answer.
- Unit mapping uses the SM files in `work/sm/fr/` (chapter and unit as named there; SM section numbers inside a chapter are used only where checked).

**How marks work (important).** Each paper prints Part I = 15 MCQs x 2 = 30 marks, all compulsory. Part II prints Q1 (14, compulsory) plus five choice questions Q2-Q6 (14 each); a candidate answers Q1 + any 4 of Q2-Q6. So a candidate **attempts 100 marks** (30 + 14 + 4 x 14), but the **marks set on the paper** are larger. Weightage below is on *marks set*. A topic in Part I or Q1 is certain to be attempted (marked **Compulsory**); a topic in Q2-Q6 is attempted only if the student chooses that question (marked Choice).

**Check (printed marks total = 30 + Q1 + five choice questions).** All three papers pass; nothing was unreadable.

The scenarios always combine several adjustments: NCI at fair value (all three), fair-value uplift or write-down of identifiable assets (machinery, brand, PPE and bonds, Vax-Shield), intra-group balances (bills, receivable/payable), unrealised profit (equipment in Jan 2026, inventory in May 2026), and acquisition-date mechanics (step acquisition in Sep 2025 and May 2026; deferred consideration, shares issued and goodwill impairment in Jan 2026). May 2026 also asks journal entries for the business combination before the balance sheet. ICAI's May 2026 answer ends in goodwill of 10,50,000 (NCI at fair value 16,00,000), a 2,50,000 gain on the earlier 30% stake and 20,000 unrealised profit on inventory; Sep 2025's answer ended in a bargain purchase (capital reserve).

The core skill is the same: discount at the straight-debt market rate, residual to equity, effective-interest finance cost. In May 2026 ICAI measures the liability on cash flows to the put date (put at 5% premium after year 3), and the equity component is not recycled to profit or loss on exercise but transferred within equity.

**3. Ind AS 115 (21 marks, exactly 7 every paper).** Every paper has a 5-mark Q5(a) plus one or two MCQs. # AFM writing-practice plan, 26 Oct to 3 Nov 2026

Exam: 4 Nov 2026. All marks, question labels and question text are from the ICAI papers. The schedule, timings, concept labels, formula drills and checklist are **app-written plan**. Nothing here restates question text: the app shows the full question from the ICAI file named in the last table.

## Assumptions and rules

- **Assumption (scale as needed):** 90 minutes of AFM handwriting per day, in two blocks of 45 minutes (Block A, Block B). On 3 Nov the plan is a lighter 60 minutes (two blocks of 30).
- **Timing yardstick:** 1.8 minutes per mark (ICAI: 100 marks in 180 minutes). Minutes per exercise = marks x 1.8, rounded to the nearest minute (4 marks = 7, 5 = 9, 6 = 11, 7 = 13, 8 = 14, 10 = 18).
- Each block starts with an 8-minute formula drill (write the key formulas of that day's chapter from memory, then check against the SM chapter text in `work/sm/afm/`). The remaining minutes in a block are 'compare and tidy' time.
- **Modes:** *copy* = copy the ICAI model answer neatly (formula first, then substitution, units, boxed result). *from-memory* = read the question and the ICAI answer, close it, write it again, compare. *timed* = blank sheet, 1.8 min per mark, then compare. *full-paper* = whole ICAI-style paper under the clock.
- **Days 7 and 8 are full 3-hour papers** (180 minutes, Nov 2026 MTP Series I and II), which is an exception to the 90-minute day. If 3 hours is not available, do the 90-minute sectional given under each day (50 marks x 1.8 = 90 minutes). Marking against the ICAI answers is done separately and is not counted.
- May 2026 questions now have ICAI suggested answers (`work/papers/afm_may26_sa_1.txt`), so they are used for from-memory and timed work and compared with ICAI's answer. For May 2026 MCQs ICAI gives only an answer key (MCQ 6 of Case Scenario II says 'No correct option'). RTPs print no marks, so no RTP question is used in the timed plan.
- Priority follows the analysis (afm-last3-analysis.md): Ch 9 (45 marks), Ch 10 (41), Ch 6 (38), Ch 8 (37), Ch 5 (34), Ch 14 (29), Ch 11 (25), Ch 12 (21). Repeat codes R1 to R18 refer to the repeat list there.

## Hand and format checklist (app-written)

- Question number written legibly in the margin and at the start of each answer; sub-part labels (a), (i) kept.
- Working notes labelled and kept with the answer; one clean table per working, ruled columns, total line underlined.
- Formula first, then substitution, then result; units (` lakh, crore, %, per unit) on every figure.
- Final answer boxed or underlined; the decision sentence (buy/hold/sell, which option, accept/reject) written after the box.
- Leave 2 blank lines between sub-parts; do not squeeze, so later corrections fit.
- Write at your natural speed, not faster than you can read back; check figures copied from the question once.
- Use the same pen and writing position as in the exam; sit upright; relax the grip every 20 minutes.
- Round only at the end unless the question says otherwise; follow the stated decimal places.
- Theory answers: short numbered points, one line each, underline the key term.

## 0. How to read this file, and what could not be fully verified

- **Sources.** Sep 2025 and Jan 2026: ICAI papers with suggested answers (`work/papers/aaa_sep25_qp_2.txt`, `aaa_jan26_qp_2.txt`). May 2026: ICAI suggested answers (`work/papers/aaa_may26_sa_1.txt`, published after the first draft of this file; marks confirmed against the scanned question paper `aaa_may26_qp_1.pdf`, all 32 pages read as images). May 2026 concepts now cite the SA, section or clause that ICAI's answer uses.
- **MCQs.** ICAI's answer key gives only the option letter (no reasoning, no standard). MCQ concepts are therefore taken from the question and option wording. One row per MCQ (2 marks each) is used instead of one row per case scenario, because each scenario mixes chapters. ## Hand and format checklist (app-written)

- Posture and grip: relaxed grip, forearm resting on the desk, shake out the hand every 20-25 minutes; use the same pen type you will use in the exam, and carry spares.
- Question number written legibly at the start of every answer (the paper's own instruction says this), sub-part labels as printed, e.g. Q2(b)(i).
- Three-step layout for scenario answers: (1) provision (the clause / SA / section, quoted by number); (2) analysis (apply it to the facts given, using the names in the question); (3) conclusion (one line, answering exactly what was asked).
- Underline SA numbers, clause numbers and Schedule references; leave a line between sub-parts.
- Working notes form part of the answer (printed on the paper); keep them under the answer.
- Marks drive length: about 9 minutes and roughly 20-25 lines for 5 marks; about 7 minutes and 15-18 lines for 4 marks. (Line counts are an app-written rule of thumb, adjust to your handwriting.)
- Speed: after each COPY or MEMORY exercise write down actual minutes taken next to the yardstick; if you are over by more than 20%, shorten the analysis, never skip the conclusion.
- Never leave a question blank; write the provision and the conclusion even if the analysis is short.
